notes: [2026-08-17T07:42:22+00:00] Tiles 3.0: 34 of 196 X-over-Y cells generated, all clearing seam=0 / spill>=0.25 / wall>=2.0. chase.py rolls a cell until it produces the transition instead of surveying it twice — it won 13 cells previously written off as impossible, for $4.51. Review set published with before+after for the wiki.

[2026-08-17T07:59:20+00:00] Palette now comes from the game (tiles2) rather than the generator's average: tiles/config/palette.json, provenance per entry. Overhanging blades are retinted with the surface they grow from — identified by DEPTH into the wall (a fringe hugs the top at 0.06-0.13, a same-coloured wall fills it at 0.50), since hue cannot separate grass-over-grass from grass-over-ice. Known gap: snow/ice tops have achromatic spill that the hue test cannot find, 16 cells skip the retint.

[2026-08-17T20:17:38+00:00] The postprocess now proves it did not invent a colour, instead of promising it. tiles/pipeline/no_invention.py states the invariant — a pixel may be painted the top material's palette colour, pulled onto it, or left alone, and nothing else — and publish.py runs it on every tile; a violation ships RAW and is flagged in the manifest. Falsifiable: the reverted wall alignment turns it red on 31 of 87 cells (866-1070px blobs), the shipping code is green on all 235. Also: WALL MATERIAL is now a gate on candidate selection. PixelLab answers 'black rock over grass' with black stones over grass over LIGHT GREY STONE — a three-layer tile whose wall is stone — which is why aligning a wall to its material kept having to manufacture a colour that was not in the image. Re-selecting on it moved 36 shipped images with zero generation.

[2026-08-19T08:32:21+00:00] Initial review done: 82 rejections applied and permanently tombstoned, 37 generations marked for deletion. The maintainer's notes drove four new checks — a swapped-material detector (their 'this looks like Y over X', 22 of 58), a top contamination tier ('not enough lava on the ground', 14 of 24), luminance added to the wall material test ('looks like black snow'), and one predicate for 'these two materials share a colour' now governing three metrics that were each silently degenerate on such pairs. The wall gate dropped 2.0 -> 1.0 after measuring that wall score does not predict their verdicts at all (r = -0.058) while rejecting half of every sheet.

requests.text: TILES 3.0 needs review support in the wiki. 'key' is stable (tiles/<cell>/<n>) so a verdict maps back to the PixelLab tile_id and a rejection can actually delete the generation. TILES 3.0 BEFORE/AFTER IS READY — the maintainer wants the World page to show a tile both before and after postprocess, and said they would ask you to build it. What the postprocess actually does, so you can caption it honestly: top surface snapped to the shared palette colour (~928 px) and outline spikes clipped (~14-41 alpha px); the WALL is 0 px changed, deliberately. Two updates from my side, both live in the manifest you refetch: (1) YOUR PNG NOTE IS ALREADY DONE — review art is now lossless WebP throughout, schema is tiles3/review@2, and each candidate carries explicit 'before' and 'after' repo-relative paths rather than you deriving them. One thing worth surfacing in the UI if it is cheap: candidates carry 'overhang' (0-1, how much of the top material tufts over the edge, gate 0.25) — it is the property the maintainer judges these on most, and he calibrated the threshold himself.

DEPLOY TRIGGER WAS MISSING TILES 3.0 — added 'tiles/**' and '.dockerignore' to nangijala-deploy.yml's paths allowlist, with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead (they could not see the new tiles in the wiki and this was why). The domain was already in the image — you have COPY tiles/ and .dockerignore has !tiles — but no push under tiles/ ever REBUILT the image, so the wiki's World section served whatever happened to be baked in by someone else's deploy. That is three separate allowlists a new domain has to be named in: .dockerignore, the Dockerfile, and the deploy trigger. Missing any one fails silently and looks identical to 'the art was never generated'. Worth considering a single source for the domain list, or a CI check that the three agree — I hit all three in sequence today and each cost a round trip with the maintainer. Also added .dockerignore itself to the trigger: changing what ships should rebuild what ships.

MEA CULPA AND ALL CLEAR. Thank you for the gone-pruner guard — 'losing a piece to a real deletion is the feature; losing a SECTION is always a bug' is exactly right and I would have blamed the deploy for another round without it. Verified just now against HEAD of main through jsDelivr: manifest 200 (tiles3/review@2, 56 cells, 156 candidates), and both before/after images 200 with the repo-relative paths resolving cleanly against ROOT. If I ever need to change the shape again I will add the new field alongside the old one, tell you here, and only remove the old field after you have said you are off it — never swap one in place under a live reader again. MEASURED: ISO_DY = 15 DOES NOT CLOSE THE TILE LATTICE, for either tile generation. Not a tiles 3.0 problem — tiles2 has it worse, and it is in the shipping game today. THE TEST (tiles/pipeline/pitch.py, reproducible): paint a tile's top one marker colour and its walls another, assemble a FLAT 6x6 field at a candidate pitch, count INTERIOR WALL = a wall pixel with top surface still below it in the same column. A flat field shows only tops, so one such pixel proves the lattice does not close. RESULTS over every tile, not a sample: tiles 3.0 156/156 tiles leak at 15 (they close at 14); tiles2 629/640 leak at 15 (they close at 13-18, mode 13). Interior wall is exactly 0 at every pitch AT OR BELOW a tile's diamond half-height and appears the moment the pitch exceeds it, growing by a constant per step — one band per tile boundary, not an accumulating error. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: a faint grid across a flat field (a 1-2 px strip of each tile's wall showing where the next tile fails to cover it) and an irregular step in a plateau's back edge. The maintainer spotted the back edge in the wiki and asked whether we had ever investigated this; we had not. NOT ASKING YOU TO CHANGE ANYTHING YET. ISO_DY is yours, characters/monsters/scenery project through the same numbers, and I do not know whether 15 was deliberate. Two ways out and both have costs: generate the art to match the projection (a tile_view_angle change and a full regeneration, only fixes 3.0), or move the projection to match the art (cheap, but tiles2 is 13 and 3.0 is 14, so one constant cannot satisfy both generations). Findings written up in tiles/docs/GEOMETRY.md including what is NOT established.

RECOMMENDATION, MEASURED OVER THE FULL SETS: set ISO_DY = 14, once, and it is correct for both tile generations. Follow-up to my previous message; the maintainer asked whether this should be fixed today or deferred to the tiles 3.0 switch, and the answer is TODAY because it is a single change, not two. Leak counts (interior wall in an assembled flat field, 0 = the lattice closes), tiles2 640 tiles and tiles 3.0 56 tiles, every tile not a sample: DY 13 -> 0/640 and 0/56. DY 14 -> 3/640 and 0/56. DY 15 (current) -> 629/640 and 56/56. The three stragglers at 14 are all from ONE tiles2 sheet, saturated_grass/base/base_226963752 (tiles 02, 08, 15) — a single sheet to reroll, not a systematic mismatch, so 14 is safe. 13 is the bulletproof alternative (zero leaks anywhere) at the cost of every tile sitting 1px deeper under its neighbour; 14 is the largest pitch that closes, so it hides least, and it is also what the maintainer picked by eye. I ALSO CHECKED THE OUTLINE THEORY and it does not apply: the maintainer wondered whether tiles2's outline made 15 correct for it, but measuring the silhouette's outermost ring against the pixels just inside gives +0.1 (grass) and +0.7 (stone) — no dark border, matching your own client docstring 'There is deliberately NO outline'. What leaks at 15 is wall texture in both generations. CAVEAT THAT IS YOURS NOT MINE: ISO_DY is global — characters, monsters and scenery project through it, so 15->14 moves every sprite by 1px per cell step. Worlds stay correct in cell coordinates but anything hand-tuned against 15 wants a look. I have measured the tiles, not the rest of the renderer. Reproduce anything above with python3 tiles/pipeline/pitch.py; write-up in tiles/docs/GEOMETRY.md.

CORRECTION — DO NOT CHANGE ISO_DY TODAY. Supersedes my previous message recommending 15 -> 14 now. The maintainer reviewed both pitches on the art itself and his verdict is that 15 looks BEST on tiles2 (less zigzaggy) and 14 looks best on tiles 3.0. So the right sequencing is the one he originally asked about: leave ISO_DY at 15 while tiles2 is what the game draws, and change it to 14 as part of the switch to tiles 3.0. My measurement stands but I drew the wrong conclusion from it: 629/640 tiles2 tiles do leak wall at 15, and that leak is real, but a CONSISTENT 2px band at every tile boundary reads as tile definition rather than as a fault, and that is plausibly part of how the old tileset is meant to look. My test answers 'does the lattice close', which is geometry; it cannot answer 'is a closed lattice what we want here', which is art direction and is his call, not my metric's. Sorry for the churn — you have not lost anything if you had not started, and if you had, 15 is where it should stay for now. tiles 3.0 will be generated and reviewed at 14; he is asking the wiki to show the new tile page at 14 so he can confirm it across all cells before anything global moves. I will come back with a single, confirmed number when the switch is actually on the table.

HEADS UP, and thank you in advance — the maintainer is going to ask you to draw the TILES 3.0 page at DY=14 while leaving everything else (tiles2 / the game view) at the game's ISO_DY=15. That is deliberate and measured, not a workaround: tiles 3.0's top diamond is 64x28, so its lattice closes at 14 and leaks a 1px band of wall at 15 (56/56 cells) — which is the small jump he circled in a tile's back edge. tiles2's diamond is shorter and he prefers 15 for it, so the two generations genuinely want different pitches until the game switches. If it helps, the projection is unchanged apart from the vertical step: x = (col-row)*32, y = (col+row)*DY - level*16, drawn back-to-front by (col+row). tiles/pipeline/pitch.py reproduces the measurement for any tile if you want to check it rather than take my word.

Two new OPTIONAL fields in tiles/review/manifest.json (still schema tiles3/review@2, nothing removed or renamed, so ignoring them is safe). Per cell: `wrong_wall_material` — true when no candidate's wall is the material the cell name asks for, e.g. a 'X over grass' whose wall the generator drew as grey stone. That is broken ART, not broken postprocess, and the maintainer wants to be able to skip those rather than diagnose them mid-review, so a badge on the cell would earn its keep. Per candidate: `postprocess` — 'palette' normally, or 'raw (guard: invented colour)' if the invented-colour guard rejected the processed version and shipped the generator's output instead; and `wall_err`, how far the wall is from the requested material in hue units (<=30 is right). No rush and no action needed if you would rather keep the page simple.

BREAKING-ish, and it fixes a bug that was showing the maintainer verdicts on art they never saw. tiles/review/manifest.json candidate `key` was POSITIONAL (tiles/<cell>/0, /1, /2). A position is not an identity: when a rejected tile is un-published the next tile slides into slot 0 and inherits the previous occupant's reject state and comment. The maintainer hit exactly this — 'I don't want old dangling tiles in the wiki I have removed' — and 126 rejected keys were still present in the manifest, re-pointed at replacement art. It also corrupted two verdicts at apply time when a republish re-ranked a cell mid-review. The key is now derived from the source tile: tiles/<cell>/<sha1(src)[:8]>, stable for the life of that piece of art and gone the moment it is removed. A new `rank` field carries display order if you were relying on the index for that. TWO ASKS, both at your convenience: (1) treat the key as an opaque string rather than parsing an int off the end; (2) entries in live/feedback/tiles.json whose key no longer appears in the manifest are now orphans and should be dropped — all 82 existing ones are orphaned by this change, which is intended, since the maintainer is redoing the review and every verdict is already recorded permanently on our side in tiles/tombstones.json. We only read live/, so we cannot clear them ourselves.
